key_insight: Low-dimensional capping makes 3D perovskite surfaces rougher while improving photoluminescence and preserving electronic uniformity, even under accelerated aging.
engineering_relevance: Surface smoothness alone is an unreliable quality metric for these heterostructures; capping offers a route to more optoelectronically stable photovoltaic materials.
method: Cap 3D perovskites with Ruddlesden–Popper layers derived from 5-tert-butyl-phenanthridinium.
Combine statistical atomic force microscopy with spatially resolved confocal photoluminescence spectroscopy.
Compare morphology, emission, and quasi-Fermi level splitting before and after accelerated aging.
evidence_signal: Despite increased roughness and height asymmetry, capped films showed enhanced photoluminescence, reduced non-radiative recombination, and more uniform radiative quasi-Fermi level splitting than pristine films.
watch_item: The abstract provides no quantitative device-efficiency or operational-lifetime results, so photovoltaic performance gains remain unverified here.
paper_title: Electronic-morphological decoupling in mixed-dimensional halide perovskite heterostructures
